title: Focus Fortnight: Exec Bridge & All-Staff Compact
body:
Purpose:
A short, focused 2-week alignment sprint for the company to (a) converge on priority OKR hypotheses for the upcoming quarter, (b) rehearse and finalize the Q2 exec update narrative, and (c) run a compact all-staff session that surfaces cross-team risks and immediate execution needs.

Why a Focus Fortnight?
- We have several competing priorities across Hosted API scaling, Dedicated capacity contracts, and Private deployment compliance updates.
- Small, time-boxed alignment reduces long tail debates; forces concrete commitments and handoffs.
- Build a repeatable cadence: fortnight-long alignment, with three internal 72-hour micro-sprints during the period for rapid decisioning.

Outcomes (must-haves by end of fortnight):
1) Draft OKRs for product + eng that are sized (success metrics + initial owners) and ready for exec sign-off.
2) A 12-slide exec update (speaker notes) and one-page TL;DR for external partners.
3) A prioritized cross-team risk register with owners and mitigation steps for the next 60 days.
4) Clear rollout plan for one low-risk Dedicated capacity pricing change and one experimental Optimize feature (A/B flag plan).

Structure & Schedule (two weeks):
- Day 0 (pre-start): Share baseline materials (usage metrics, latency/cost trends, customer signals).
- Days 1-3 (Micro-sprint A - OKR scoping): product, eng, research, and finance workshop; produce OKR hypotheses.
- Days 4-7 (Micro-sprint B - Execution plans): owners convert OKR hypotheses to 30/60/90 execution arcs + risks.
- Days 8-10 (Micro-sprint C - Exec prep): condense into exec update, rehearse.
- Day 11 (All-staff compact, 90 minutes): present TL;DR, decision moments, Q&A; collect final feedback.
- Day 12 (Buffer / follow-ups): finalize sign-offs and publish.

Draft OKR Examples (starter ideas):
- Objective 1: Make hosted inference 2x cheaper for mid-tail request distributions without increasing p95 latency.
  - KR1: Reduce per-token cost for bursty chat workloads by 45% in internal benchmark suite.
  - KR2: Keep end-to-end p95 latency <= 250ms at 95th percentile of production traffic during peak hours.
  - Owner: eng-serving-runtime + product-hosted-api

- Objective 2: Enable enterprise-grade Private deployments for regulated customers with predictable SLOs.
  - KR1: Complete on-prem/in-cloud hardened deploy template and KMS integration for two pilot customers.
  - KR2: Document and automate audit log export to customer S3/HSM workflows.
  - Owner: private-deployments + security-and-compliance

- Objective 3: Reduce cost-per-embedding for vector search customers via caching and quantization guidance.
  - KR1: Ship Optimize recommendation engine for at least two workload archetypes and measure cost delta.
  - Owner: optimize + applied-ml

All-Staff Compact Agenda (90 minutes):
- 0–5m: Context & cadence (CEO note)
- 5–20m: One-page product + metrics snapshot (10 slides condensed)
- 20–40m: Top 3 cross-company decisions we need (each owner 5m)
- 40–60m: Quick breakout polls (async follow-ups) and risk register sprint
- 60–80m: Live Q&A (prioritized from Slack pre-asks)
- 80–90m: Action roll call + next steps

Execution Play Examples (short):
- Dedicated capacity pricing tweak: product ops owns rollout; pricing experiment flagged to 5% of eligible customers, monitor usage delta + churn signal.
- Optimize: ship a beta of batching/caching advisor in Console -> target two internal customers for pilot.

Key Data & Attachments to Share Day 0:
- Week-over-week token spend by customer segment (CSV)
- Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) across models and regions (Graph PNG)
- Cost-per-token by model variant + quantization profile (sheet)
- Customer signal highlights (support ticket excerpts, sales notes)

Decision Rules (how we accept/reject OKRs):
- Acceptance requires a single measurable KR, a named owner, and a risk mitigation note.
- If an OKR increases platform cost >10% without a clear revenue/retention gain, it must include a compensating cost-savings KR.

Risks & Pre-emptive Mitigations (top 5 at start):
1) Capacity constraints for Dedicated pools during experiments -> Mitigation: reserve burst GPU windows + automatic fallback routing to hosted variants.
2) Quantization quality regressions -> Mitigation: hold small eval sets and rollback flag in console.
3) Compliance gating for Private pilots -> Mitigation: prioritize KMS integration and audit export automation.
4) Exec bandwidth mismatch -> Mitigation: pre-read packet + recorded dry run for leadership.
5) Customer confusion on pricing changes -> Mitigation: customer comms templates + staged rollout.

Ownership & Communication Rituals:
- Daily standup channel: #focus-fortnight (eng/product/ops only) with 10–15m sync 9:30am PT.
- Decision repo: Confluence page CONFLUENCE-4482 (link above).
- Final docs to be published to /company/misc and emailed one-pager to all staff.

Immediate To-dos (first 48 hours):
- [Avery] Publish baseline packet and invite list to execs (by end of Day 0).
- [Maya] Coordinate dataset exports and metrics owners for Day 0 attachments.
- [Diego] Draft OKR template and pre-fill two starter hypotheses.
- [Sonal] Draft All-staff compact agenda + Slack pre-ask form.

Open Questions (to resolve in Micro-sprint A):
- Do we lock the Hosted API cost-savings OKR before enterprise sales pricing changes?
- Which two customers for Private pilot do we prioritize given legal/compliance timelines?
- Is the Optimize beta ready for console-based toggles or CLI-only pilot?

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact. The goal is rapid alignment with a bias to action; expect several follow-up micro-docs for each OKR.
- Please leave comments inline on the Confluence draft (CONFLUENCE-4482) or ping me in Slack if you need synchronous time.

Appendix: Quick rehearsal checklist for the Exec update
- One-slide TL;DR with top 3 asks
- 12-slide deck with speaker notes (2 slides per major area: Hosted, Dedicated, Private, Console/Optimize, Risks/Asks)
- Rehearsal slot booked: Day 9, 11am PT (leadership-only dry run)

-- Avery
